## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One critical defect needs fixing first: the new `finished_at` column holds the time a process *started*, and only while it is still running. For every process whose latest event is `started`, that timestamp is published as a finish time. This review traced `models/processes.sql` against the `process_events` schema and seed rows in `sources/process_events.sql`, and checked the new `schema.yml` description against the query. The repository has no tests or policy files, so no test exercises the new column.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the `processes` current-state model, documents it in `models/schema.yml`, and adds a one-line `review.txt` file.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Stop labelling the start time as `finished_at` — A process whose latest event is `started`, such as process 20 in `sources/process_events.sql:9`, gets `finished_at = '2026-01-01T00:01:00Z'`, but that is its start time, and the process has not finished. The expression `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` fills the column only when the latest event is `started`. The allowed event types are `'created', 'started', 'cleared'` (`sources/process_events.sql:4`), so no event marks a finish. Processes that move on to `cleared` get NULL. — Consumers reading `finished_at` will treat running processes as finished at their start time, and the column never holds a real finish time. — Fix: Decide what the column should mean. If it is a start time, rename it (for example `started_at`) and take it from the `started` event itself, not from the latest row. Otherwise the column stays NULL whenever a later event follows `started`. If it really is a finish time, it needs a source event that marks a finish, and no such event type exists today.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Fix the NULL description; NULL also covers started processes — The doc says "NULL means the process has never been started", but process 30 (`sources/process_events.sql:10-11`) was started and then cleared, and it gets `finished_at` NULL. The query returns a value only when the latest event is `started`, so any started process with a later event also reads as never started. — Consumers who rely on this documented meaning will misclassify started-then-cleared processes as never started.
